title: The New Application Layer - Malte Ubl, CTO Vercel
talk_summary: Vercel CTO Malte Ubl argues agents are a new application layer, listing four practical agent archetypes (24/7 job replacement, 'compressed research' where an agent does the research but a human still decides, surfacing existing-but-unusable company information, and eliminating hated toil). He also notes agents are becoming the majority of software users, so products need CLI/API surfaces, and that harnesses should separate where the agent runs from where generated code runs.

takeaways.what_they_do: Insert an agent only into the research phase of an existing business event → human decision process, leaving the process and risk profile unchanged; e.g. contact-sales and abuse-report triage agents at Vercel.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can just build an agent that does the research phase automatically. And that's all you do. That's all you ship
takeaways.numbers: research step 30 min → 5 min; ~75% of contact-sales messages are actually support and get rerouted

takeaways.what_they_do: Build agents that mine information already present (issue trackers, Slack, meeting recordings) to keep trackers current and answer 'status' questions proactively instead of on request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's extremely common that there's information somewhere in the company, right? But for all intents and purposes, you cannot practically use it.

takeaways.technique: Ask what people hate most, automate that first
takeaways.what_they_do: Pick agent targets by surveying the team for the most-hated toil; Vercel's in-house support agent hit 90% deflection and raised support-team job satisfaction.
takeaways.evidence_quote: ask folks, what do you hate most about your job?

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat agents as primary users: every feature must expose a CLI/API an agent can automate, not just a UI; Vercel reports agents are now the majority of its web traffic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: over 60% of page views on vercel.com were AI agents
takeaways.numbers: >60% of page views in last 7 days were AI agents

takeaways.technique: Separate harness host from generated-code execution
takeaways.what_they_do: Argue the harness (agent loop, credentials, orchestration) should not run in the same sandbox as the code the agent generates; Anthropic's new agent product reportedly adopts this split.
takeaways.evidence_quote: almost all currently popular agent harnesses have fundamentally the wrong architecture... they combine where the harness runs with where the code that it runs

takeaways.technique: Stay model-agnostic at the application layer
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a stable layer above models so swapping providers is cheap, betting on model commoditization and falling prices rather than lock-in.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this new application layer that we're building can thrive independent of the models
